description:
Find what is in imported media, or in the sound of an edit, as data for edits. transcript: every word with its time (whisper.cpp on the CPU; the model downloads once). For English the word edges are then aligned to the sound (wav2vec2 forced alignment): a word starts and ends within about 0.05 s of where its letters sound, and an end on a soft consonant (s, t, k, f) or a breath can ring on up to about 0.1 s more; timing_confidence says how clearly each word was heard. Other languages keep whisper's own times, up to about a second off. Short ums and uhs are often missing from the words, while kind speech still detects them as voice. from_seconds and until_seconds transcribe just that stretch: the words come back in the result and are not stored, so the stored transcript (which edits and captions read) stays the whole media's. file: txt also writes the transcript as a file on the cutting floor, with a download url. On a timeline_id, the words of the edit's mix. beats: tempo, beat and downbeat times, and strengths: each beat's onset strength, 0–1 of the strongest (the hardest hits, the drop); also tempo candidates (half and double time show there), a fitted tempo and bar candidates. faces: face boxes over time, e.g. to reframe to 9:16 with clip.set_transform keyframes. track: follow a region you give from a moment on, a box for each sampled time (found false where the subject was lost), as clip.set_transform or clip.set_mask keyframes for a title, sticker or mask to follow. look: your own typed questions about what is on screen, answered on every sampled frame (to find where something happens from plain words, media.seek). silence: stretches quieter than threshold_db for at least min_seconds. scenes: times the picture changes by more than threshold (0–100; hard cuts between ordinary shots score about 10 to 30, see threshold), with each cut's score. speech: the probability that someone is speaking, every 32 ms (Silero VAD), and the spans where it is at least your min_probability; it hears speech, not noise or music, so a cough or a door is not speech. loudness: integrated loudness (LUFS), true peak (dBTP), loudness range (LU), RMS level and noise floor (dBFS) over the whole media or from_seconds to until_seconds; with every_seconds, the level on steps too. To line up two recordings, media.correlate. sounds: what can be heard and when, every 40 ms, for 447 named sounds (video://catalog/sounds: Laughter, Applause, Cough, Sneeze, Music, Speech, Door, Footsteps, Beep…): give labels for the ones you want, or none for every sound that reaches your min_probability; you get each sound's spans and its probability in every frame (a run over the whole media is kept with it; one over from_seconds to until_seconds comes back only). To find a sound you describe in your own words, media.listen. Both find sounds in the media; sound effects to add come from sounds.list. speakers: who speaks when (pyannote and ERes2Net on the CPU, about 10 to 20 s a minute): turns numbered in the order voices are first heard; give speakers (how many) or cluster_threshold. Transcript words then carry their speaker. voice: pitch (YIN, Hz) and level (RMS dBFS) every 0.1 s, and a summary (pitch median and range, level, voiced seconds, words per second from the transcript), e.g. as judge.ask state. colour: per-channel mean and percentiles, luma, white point estimate and clipping (RGB 0–255) of the frame and regions you name, at sampled times. picture: FFmpeg signalstats of every frame over a stretch: luma, chroma, saturation, hue, and ydif, the change from the frame before (a flash or frozen frame shows there). onsets: where the level of any sound jumps (a hit, a clap, a note). notes: the notes one voice or instrument plays or sings (a hum, a bass line). key: a score for each of the 24 keys. spectrum: the level in third-octave bands.
With timeline_id instead of media_id, transcript, speech, loudness, silence, sounds, speakers, voice, onsets, notes, key, spectrum measure the edit's mix and faces, track, look, scenes, colour, picture its picture as it renders (titles, effects and grades included), over from_seconds to until_seconds (timeline seconds); they come back in the result. A source or range with no sound fails with no_audio, naming it.
Times are media seconds (timeline seconds for a timeline); boxes are fractions of the picture, and a box you give takes units "pixels" too (picture_size gives the size). Results stay with the media (media.get include; the latest run of each kind) except track, silence, scenes, loudness, onsets, notes, key and spectrum, which come back in the result; speech over the whole media is kept (media.get include speech), so asking again with another min_probability or range answers from it. A result too long to return (a long transcript) comes back as its summary and a note: read it in pieces with media.get include and a time range or page.
Long-running: returns a task, or a job_id for job.get.

HOW LOOK WORKS. A fast judgment model (preview) answers your questions about frames sampled from the media. Each sampled frame is its own request: the judgment model sees that one picture, named `frame`, and with with_previous also the frame sampled just before it, named `previous`, plus any state you give: text or JSON entries by name, the same on every frame (the script, what a term means). Every question is answered on every frame, independently and in parallel (about 0.15 s a frame), as typed data you then combine in your own code.
Choose the type by the answer you need. noul: yes or no, answered as noul, the probability of yes from 0 to 1. choice: one of options you name, answered as choice plus probabilities and confidence. score: a degree on levels you order, answered as score (0 is the first level; it can land between levels) plus confidence. box: where one thing is, answered as box {x, y, w, h} in fractions of the picture plus confidence.
Write each question about the picture as it looks. Name the picture in backticks ("in `frame`"), ask about one thing, word it so yes means the thing is there, and describe it as it appears: "Does `frame` show a human being, even if only their face fills the picture?", "Is one large word laid over `frame`, much bigger than any other text?". To compare, name both pictures and the thing that differs: "Is there a button in `frame` that is not in `previous`?". To locate, name the one thing so only it fits ("the 'Get started for free' button under the headline in `frame`") and, in the same call, a noul asking whether it is there; use the box on frames where that noul is high. Give a choice a none option for frames where nothing fits, and each score level a concrete situation.
Read the answers this way: a noul of 0.5 or more reads as yes, and you can set your own cut-off; confidence tells you how far to trust a choice, a score or a box, and a loose box shows as low confidence. Work in passes: every_seconds 1 over the whole media, then at_seconds around the times where answers change. media.get scenes give when the picture cuts; look tells you what is on it.
The result gives each question's spans (when a noul reads yes, which choice holds when); every frame's answers stay with the media (media.get include ['look'], the last 10 runs). Up to 600 frames and 32 questions a call. To find the moments that match a description, media.seek takes it in plain words and returns where it holds. For one judgment about text, a still or a single frame, judge.ask answers at once. Full guide to writing questions: https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives and https://docs.typesafe.ai/images.

at_seconds.description: look, colour: sample exactly these times instead

cluster_threshold.description: speakers: when the count is unknown, how different two voices must be to count as two people; lower finds more speakers (try 0.5 to 0.9)

every_seconds.description: look, colour: sample a frame this often (at least 0.04). Default 1. onsets (required): the step whose level each step is compared with the one before; loudness: also the level on steps this long (up to 20000 steps); notes: the step threshold_db compares levels on; key (at least 0.2), spectrum (at least 0.1): also per step

file.description: transcript: also write it as a file on the cutting floor, named for the media and the stretch it covers, with a download url like an export

first_bar_seconds.description: notes, with tempo: where beat 0 is, in seconds. Default 0

from_seconds.description: Start sampling or measuring here (any kind but beats, and faces and scenes on media). Default 0

kind.description: transcript: words with times (whisper.cpp, then aligned to the sound); on a timeline_id, the words of the edit's mix in timeline seconds, not kept. beats: tempo, beat times, the onset strength at each, tempo candidates, a fitted tempo and bar candidates; faces: face boxes over time; track: follow a region; look: your own questions answered on sampled frames; silence: stretches quieter than threshold_db for min_seconds; scenes: times the picture changes by more than threshold; speech: where someone is speaking (Silero VAD probability every 32 ms, spans at or above min_probability); loudness: integrated loudness, true peak, loudness range, RMS and noise floor, and with every_seconds the level on steps; sounds: when each of 447 named sounds (laughter, applause, cough, music, speech, door…) can be heard, every 40 ms; speakers: who speaks when; voice: pitch, level and pace over time; colour: colour statistics of frames and regions; picture: every frame's brightness, colour and change from the frame before. onsets: every step of every_seconds whose level (RMS dBFS) rises by threshold_db or more over the step before, for any sound (a hit, a clap, a note, a shout): its time, the rise, the level reached and its share below 250 Hz (low), 250 Hz to 4 kHz (mid) and above 4 kHz (high). notes: the notes one voice or instrument plays or sings (a hum, a whistle, a bass line), from a YIN pitch line (40 Hz to 2 kHz, every 10 ms, 50 ms median): start, end, Hz, nearest note name (equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz), cents off it and level; with tempo, in beats too. A new note starts where the pitch moves split_cents from the note's mean so far, or with threshold_db and every_seconds where the level rises that much (a note struck again on one pitch); notes shorter than min_seconds are left out. It follows one line: on several instruments at once, the loudest (create.stems separates them). key: a score 0–1 for each of the 24 major and minor keys, and the strength of each of the 12 note names (C2 to C8), over the range and with every_seconds per step. spectrum: the level in dB of each third-octave band from 20 Hz to 20 kHz (sound mixed to one channel), over the range and with every_seconds per step. onsets, notes, key and spectrum take from_seconds and until_seconds (up to 7200 s for onsets, 600 for notes, 3600 for key and spectrum) and come back whole in the result, not kept with the media: up to 5000 onsets, 2000 notes, 5000 key and 2000 spectrum steps a call

labels.description: sounds: the sounds to report, named as in video://catalog/sounds (e.g. ["Laughter", "Applause", "Cough"]). Default: every sound that reaches min_probability somewhere

min_probability.description: speech (required): a 32 ms frame with at least this speech probability is speech; sounds (required): a 40 ms frame has the sound when its probability is at least this

min_seconds.description: silence (required): only stretches at least this long. notes (required): notes shorter than this are left out

model.description: transcript: whisper size, on the server CPU. Bigger is more accurate and slower: small takes about 3 times as long as base, tiny about half

percentiles.description: colour: the percentiles to give of each channel

questions.description: look: id (yours, not shown to the model) to question; up to 32, all asked of every frame

region.description: track: the box to follow (top-left x, y and size) and when

units.description: fraction (default): of the picture; pixels: of the picture at its own size
fraction (default): of the picture; pixels: of the picture at its own size

regions.description: colour: named boxes to measure besides the whole frame (frame), up to 16

speakers.description: speakers: how many people speak, when you know (or give cluster_threshold)

split_cents.description: notes (required): a new note starts where the pitch moves this many cents (100 a semitone) from the note's mean so far

state.description: look: text or JSON entries shown beside `frame` on every frame, by name, for questions to refer to (a script line, a definition)

tempo.description: notes: beats per minute, to give each note in beats too

threshold.description: scenes (required): how much the picture must change to count as a cut, 0–100 (FFmpeg scdet's score): the change from the frame before, in percent of full range, less the change just before it (so steady motion stays low). Hard cuts between ordinary shots score about 10 to 30, a cut between opposite pictures up to 100: start at FFmpeg's own default, 10, and raise it if you get too many

threshold_db.description: silence (required): quieter than this counts as silence, dBFS (-100 to 0). onsets (required): a step counts when its level is at least this many dB over the step before (above 0). notes: a new note also starts where the level rises this much over the step before, on steps of every_seconds

timeline_id.description: Analyze an edit as it plays (timeline seconds): its mix (transcript, speech, loudness, silence, sounds, speakers, voice, onsets, notes, key, spectrum) or its picture (faces, track, look, scenes, colour, picture)

until_seconds.description: Stop sampling or measuring here. Default: the end

with_previous.description: look: also show the frame sampled before, as `previous`

name: media.analyze

job_id.description: Job handle; the same value is the MCP task id

media_id.description: The media it is making: an import is usable in edits once its status is processing, a created media once this job completes

result.description: The result, when status is completed; otherwise job.get gives it once completed

bar_candidates.description: For bars of 2 to 7 beats: each beat a bar could start on, with the accent behind it

accent.description: Mean onset strength of every beat at that place in the bar, as strengths

beat.description: Index in beats of the first beat a bar could start on

fitted_bpm.description: The tempo the beat times keep: 60 over the slope of a straight line through them

strengths.description: Per beat: its onset strength, 0–1 of the strongest in the sound

tempo_candidates.description: Every tempo from 30 to 300 BPM the onsets repeat at (a peak of the tracker’s tempo strength, with no lean to any tempo), strongest first, 0–1 of the strongest: half and double time show here

clipped_high.description: Share of pixels with a channel at 255

clipped_low.description: Share of pixels black in every channel

luma.description: Rec. 709 luma of the encoded values: 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B

pixels.description: The region measured, in pixels of the picture

white_point.description: Mean colour of the brightest 1% of its pixels, an estimate of the white point

regions.description: frame: the whole picture; and each region you named

items.description: Top-left corner x, y and size w, h, fractions of the picture (centre: x + w/2, y + h/2); score 0–1

expiry.description: When the file goes, in words

page_url.description: Shows the file in any browser

notes.description: Per note name (C, C#, … B): its strength over the range, 0–1 of the strongest

scores.description: Per key ("C major" … "B minor", 24): 0–1, how well the note strengths match the key (Krumhansl–Kessler profile correlation r, as (r + 1) / 2)

notes.description: Per step: the 12 strengths, C first, 0–1 of that step’s strongest; null: silent, or no window is centred in it

look.description: look: this run (id, model, questions, frames with answers)

channels.description: Each channel on its own, in stream order (1 is left in stereo)

integrated_lufs.description: EBU R128; null below its -70 LUFS gate

noise_floor_dbfs.description: Level of the quietest moments (FFmpeg astats noise floor): room tone or hiss

rms_dbfs.description: RMS level over the whole stretch

steps.description: With every_seconds: the level on steps

level_db.description: Per step: RMS dBFS over every channel; null: digital silence

until.description: Seconds measured until; null: the end

media_id.description: Media handle from media.import or a create.* tool

note.description: In place of the analysis when it is too long to return: where to read it

method.description: The pitch line: YIN, 40 Hz to 2 kHz, every 10 ms, 50 ms median

note.description: Nearest note name, equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz, C4 middle C

start_beats.description: With tempo: beats from first_bar_seconds (0 is its first beat)

onsets.description: In time order; the first step has none before it

low.description: Share of the step below 250 Hz, 0–1

rise_db.description: Its level less the step before, dB; null: the step before was digital silence

time.description: Where the step that rose starts

columns.description: One number per frame in each, in order: time, then FFmpeg signalstats in the picture's own bit depth (0–255 for 8-bit): ymin, ylow (10th percentile), yavg, yhigh (90th), ymax, the same for u and v, satmin…satmax, huemed, hueavg, ydif, udif, vdif (mean change from the frame before), and the bits each plane uses (ybitdepth…)

picture_size.description: faces, track, colour: the picture measured, in pixels (a box times it is pixels)

scene_scores.description: scenes: how much the picture changed at each cut, on the threshold scale

silences.description: silence: media seconds; a stretch after the sound stops (see sound_ends) counts as silent

sound_ends.description: silence: where the sound stream stops, when it stops before the media ends: past it there is no sound at all

peaks.description: Per sound reported: the highest probability it reaches anywhere

scores.description: Every probability, for your own cut-off or arithmetic

start_seconds.description: Where the first value starts: media seconds, or timeline seconds for a timeline

step_seconds.description: Seconds each value covers: 0.04 (every frame) unless asked or too long

values.description: Per sound, the highest probability in each step, 0 to 1

end.description: Where it ends, on the same clock

peak_seconds.description: The middle of the most likely frame

start.description: Where the run of matching 40 ms frames starts: media seconds, or timeline seconds for a timeline

spans.description: Per sound: the runs of 40 ms frames at or above min_probability, in time order; empty when it never is

cluster_threshold.description: The cut-off you gave, or null

from.description: The stretch diarised, when not the whole media

speakers_asked.description: The count you gave, or null

turns.description: Each stretch of one voice, by start; two voices at once overlap

confidence.description: 0–1: how close this turn's voice sits to its speaker's other turns

speaker.description: 0 is the first voice heard, 1 the next new one, …

bands_hz.description: Third-octave band centres, 20 Hz to 20 kHz

level_db.description: Per band over the range: RMS dBFS of what lies in it; null: nothing
Per step, per band; null: no window is centred in the step

probabilities.description: Every frame, when short enough to return; media: also media.get include speech

spans.description: Runs of frames at or above min_probability, seconds

summary.description: The summary media.get gives under analyses; look: where each answer holds

timeline_id.description: Timeline handle; every edit returns a new one

aligned_by.description: The model that moved word edges to where the letters sound (English); null: the times are whisper's own, up to about a second off

from.description: The stretch transcribed, if not all

words.description: Media seconds. Aligned words start and end within about 0.05 s of where their letters sound; an end on a soft consonant (s, t, k, f) or a breath can ring on up to about 0.1 s more. Short ums are often missing from the words; kind speech finds them as speech. A word "-" (or one starting with it) is whisper marking a new speaker, as subtitles do: a hint only; kind speakers measures who speaks when

confidence.description: 0–1: how sure whisper is of the word itself

speaker.description: Who says it, from the latest speakers run

timing_confidence.description: 0–1: how clearly the letters were heard between start and end; null: not aligned (digits, symbols, other languages), times fitted between neighbours

pitch_hz.description: Median of its voiced 10 ms steps; null: none

voiced.description: Share of it with a clear pitch, 0–1

pitch_range_semitones.description: p10 to p90: how much the voice moves

voiced_seconds.description: Time with a clear pitch: voice, not noise or silence

words.description: Transcript words in the stretch; null: no transcript

title: Analyze media
